investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~149 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap failure for all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~149 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap failure for all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 13:07 and 13:12 UTC on 2026-07-07 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Every new remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was immediately marked Unschedulable and remained stuck for ~145–149 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or broader service impact is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by all three sibling check messages reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the same 2 nodes.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is reduced even when total cluster resources appear sufficient.

TERTIARY — no preemption victims available: the scheduler message explicitly states 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free VM slots. This is a consequence of the primary cause but could also indicate missing PriorityClass configuration on the eval pods.

LOW PROBABILITY — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent usage by other tenants consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the exact time the eval ran. This would be a timing coincidence rather than a structural capacity problem, but cannot be ruled out without cluster utilization history.
